stories.headline: TEN-YEAR YIELD HITS 4.63%, HIGHEST SINCE JAN 2025 — RATE HIKE ODDS HARDEN
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed 8 bps to 4.63% Monday, its highest level since January 2025, as the Iran conflict kept WTI above $106 and inflation expectations elevated. Markets are now pricing a 45%+ probability of at least one Fed rate hike in 2026-27 — up from near zero a month ago — with new Chair Kevin Warsh facing his first major policy test.

stories.headline: WTI HOLDS $106 AS TRUMP WARNS IRAN: 'THE CLOCK IS TICKING'
stories.body: WTI crude held above $106 per barrel Monday — Brent above $110 — after Iran submitted amended peace terms to the Trump administration. President Trump publicly warned that 'the Clock is Ticking' for Tehran to accept. The ongoing supply-risk premium in oil is the primary driver of elevated headline CPI and the bond market's inflation repricing.

stories.headline: EMPIRE STATE MANUFACTURING SURGES TO 19.6 VS. 7 EXPECTED
stories.body: The NY Empire State Manufacturing Index for May printed 19.6 — more than double the consensus estimate of 7 — while April industrial production rose 0.7% with capacity utilization at 76.1%, both beating forecasts. The data complicate the Fed's calculus: growth is holding up even as energy inflation builds, reducing the argument against hiking.

stories.headline: NVIDIA EARNINGS WEDNESDAY — KEY READ ON AI CAPEX AT ELEVATED YIELDS
stories.body: Nvidia reports Wednesday, May 20, alongside Target. With the Nasdaq down 0.51% on yield pressure and tech equities under rate-sensitivity stress, Nvidia's results will determine whether AI-driven earnings growth can justify current valuations at 4.63% long rates. A miss on data center revenue guidance could accelerate the rotation out of growth.

stories.headline: MICHIGAN ATOP EARLY 76-TEAM BRACKET; NBA WITHDRAW DEADLINE MAY 27
stories.body: Reigning national champion Michigan leads Andy Katz's first projection for next season's expanded 76-team NCAA Tournament. The most consequential offseason date is May 27 — the deadline for players to withdraw from the NBA Draft and return to school — which will finalize college rosters and set off the remaining recruiting and transfer dominoes.

stories.headline: WCF GAME 1 TONIGHT: WEMBANYAMA'S SPURS VS. SGA'S THUNDER, 8:30 PM ET
stories.body: Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Oklahoma City Thunder tip off Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals tonight at 8:30 PM ET on NBC — the league's most anticipated matchup of the season. In the East, Cleveland — who ended Detroit's year with a 125-94 Game 7 blowout Sunday — opens vs. New York on Tuesday.

stories.headline: RODGERS RE-SIGNS STEELERS ON 1-YEAR DEAL UP TO $25M; OTAS BEGIN
stories.body: Aaron Rodgers officially re-signed with Pittsburgh for a 22nd NFL season on a 1-year contract worth up to $25 million — a significant raise from his $13.65M last year — and took first-team reps on the opening day of OTAs Monday. Across the league, all 32 clubs kicked off the voluntary OTA window running through early June.

stories.headline: HUSKIES MOVE IOWA, PURDUE GAMES TO FRIDAY NIGHTS; PORTAL ERA SETTLING IN
stories.body: UW's games against Iowa and at Purdue have been moved to Friday night slots in the 2026 schedule. Nationally, with spring games complete and the portal cycle closed, programs are finalizing depth charts — LSU's Lane Kiffin and Penn State's Matt Campbell assembled top-five portal classes, cementing the depth-transfer model as the dominant roster-building strategy.

deepDive.title: Energy Pass-Through: How an Oil Shock Forces the Fed's Hand
content: With WTI above $106 and the 10-year yield at its highest since January 2025, the market is pricing something unusual: rate hikes driven not by demand overheating but by a supply shock. The Iran conflict has injected a sustained energy premium into oil prices since February, and that premium is bleeding directly into headline CPI — putting the Fed in a bind it hasn't faced in years. The question for markets isn't whether inflation is real; it's whether the Fed should raise rates to fight price increases that aren't driven by excessive demand.

The oil-to-CPI transmission works through two channels. The direct channel is fast: gasoline prices rise within weeks of a crude oil shock, and energy makes up roughly 7% of the CPI basket. A 20% oil spike adds approximately 50–70 basis points to headline CPI directly. The indirect channel is slower and larger: energy is an input into nearly every good and service — trucking, manufacturing, food production, chemicals, plastics. As businesses absorb higher energy costs, they pass them through in prices over 6 to 12 months. Historical estimates suggest the full pass-through of a $20/barrel oil shock adds another 30–50 bps to core CPI over a year, meaning the total inflation impact of today's move is still unfolding.

The Fed's historical record on supply shocks is poor. During the 1973 OPEC embargo, Arthur Burns was too slow to respond — oil quadrupled, inflation hit double digits, and the Fed was behind the curve for years. Volcker's aggressive response to the 1979–80 Iranian Revolution shock — hiking the fed funds rate to 20% — broke inflation expectations but caused a severe recession. More recently, the 2021–22 energy shock from the Ukraine war added roughly three percentage points to peak CPI and contributed to the Fed's most aggressive tightening cycle since Volcker. Each episode reveals the same tradeoff: let inflation run and it gets entrenched in expectations; fight it with rate hikes and you risk overdoing it into a slowing economy.

Today's setup is particularly uncomfortable because the economy is sending mixed signals. Empire State manufacturing surprised sharply to the upside today, but that's one regional survey against a backdrop of rising yields already tightening financial conditions. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh must decide whether to validate the market's 45% hike probability or push back. The key variable is whether this is a permanent oil shock — in which case hiking makes sense — or a temporary geopolitical premium that reverses if talks succeed. If Iran and the U.S. reach a deal, oil could retreat to $80 within weeks and the entire hike narrative unwinds. That optionality is why Nvidia's guidance Wednesday matters so much — it's a referendum on whether AI earnings can carry tech at elevated discount rates.
